title: Lift the self by the self
hook: Arjuna sank down in his chariot; chapter six says the self that sinks you can lift you
carry: lift the self by the self
tomorrow: A clean place, a firm seat

segments.voice: Yesterday, shanti: the lasting peace comes from the friend of all beings that doesn't end, from the friend of all beings. Today, chapter six, the chapter of meditation, and a friend much closer to home.
screen: `SHANTI — LASTING PEACE COMES FROM THE FRIEND OF ALL BEINGS THAT DOESN'T END.`

segments.voice: Go back to the very start of the Gita. Two armies face each other. Arjuna, a great archer, looks across and sees his teachers, his cousins, his grandfather. His bow slips from his hand. He sinks down onto the seat of his chariot and says he won't fight. Everything Krishna teaches after that is an answer to that sinking. Now listen to the voice in your own head after something goes wrong. You always do this. What's wrong with you. Words you'd never say to a friend. Chapter six has two lines about that voice too.
screen: `HIS BOW SLIPS FROM HIS HAND.` → `HE SINKS DOWN IN THE CHARIOT.` → `WHAT DOES YOUR OWN VOICE SAY?`

segments.voice: First, Krishna clears something up. The true renouncer, verse one says, isn't the one who stops lighting the sacred fire or stops working. It's the one who does what needs doing without leaning on the fruit. For someone climbing toward yoga, verse three adds, action is the way up; for someone who has arrived, stillness. Then verses five and six. Lift yourself by yourself; don't let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self. In Sanskrit the same word, atman, the self, comes again and again, like a mirror facing a mirror. The word for friend is bandhu: a friend, and also kin. Here's the Hindu teaching under it. You are not your worst moment. Many teachers read the verse as the higher self lifting the lower, the steady mind lifting the scattered one. The verse doesn't say wait to be rescued, and it doesn't say you're alone; later chapters speak of grace. It says the lifting starts with your own hand. Then a portrait of the one who has done it: steady in cold and heat, praise and blame. A lump of earth, a stone and gold look alike to them. So when the inner voice piles on after you slip, the Gita's question is simple: which self is talking, the one sinking you, or the one lifting you?
screen: `THE TRUE RENOUNCER STILL ACTS.` · `LIFT YOURSELF BY YOURSELF.` · `THE SELF: FRIEND OR ENEMY.` · `YOU ARE NOT YOUR WORST MOMENT.` · then, large: `LIFT THE SELF BY THE SELF.`

segments.voice: Say the first words of verse five softly, out loud: uddhared atmanatmanam. Lift the self by the self. Now think of the last time the inner voice was harsh with you, and let the words come up. Imagine a good friend heard them said about you, and let the friend's answer come, warm. Say the line once more, and let that be the voice that answers.
Bandhu. Friend, kin: the self is its own bandhu. Gita six, five: the self is the friend of the self, and the enemy of the self. The lifting starts with your own hand.
Your line: lift the self by the self. The harsh voice doesn't get the last word. Day one hundred seventy-eight.

screen: `DAY 178 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: A CLEAN PLACE, A FIRM SEAT.`

howItsDone: Gita 6.5 ('uddhared atmanatmanam', lift the self by the self) is often learned by heart, and some Hindus recite it as encouragement in hard times.

original.note: Sanskrit: bandhu, friend or kin; from a root meaning to bind. the self is its own bandhu (6.5).

trapdoor: what you thought: pull yourself up by your bootstraps.
what it means: the self can be friend or enemy to itself; the lifting begins with your own hand, and with kindness.
what a scholar hears: 6.5, uddhared atmanatmanam, repeats atman in several cases in a single line; bandhu comes from bandh, to bind, so the friend is the one bound to you.
recall: the divine coming down in a form
